text: You are going to investigate the reaction between aqueous potassium manganate(VII), solution A,
and two solutions of iron(II) sulfate, solution B and solution C, of different concentrations.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
You are going to carry out two experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Carry out a flame test on a sample of solid E.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Pour about 10 cm of distilled water into a boiling tube. Measure the initial temperature of the
water and record it in the table. Add the rest of solid E to the boiling tube and shake the boiling
tube to dissolve solid E. Measure and record the temperature of the solution after 1 minute.
Complete the table.
temperature of the solution after 1 minute / C
initial temperature of the water / C
temperature difference / C

Divide the solution into three equal portions in three test-tubes and carry out the following tests.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
To the first portion of the solution, add about 2 cm of dilute hydrochloric acid.
Test the gas given off with a small strip of filter paper that has been dipped into
acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
To the second portion of the solution, add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide.
Record your observations.

text: You are provided with two solids, E and F, which are both salts.
Carry out the following tests on each solid, recording all of your observations at each stage.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Mix about 2 cm of aqueous copper(II) sulfate and 2 cm of aqueous potassium iodide. Add
a small amount of starch solution to the mixture. Leave the solution to stand for 5 minutes.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add the third portion of the solution of E to the mixture in (e)(i).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
What conclusions can you draw about solid E?

tests on solid F

Record your observations.

Add the rest of solid F to about 5 cm of distilled water in a test-tube. Shake the mixture to dissolve
solid F. Divide the solution into two equal portions in two test-tubes.

parts.label: (h)
parts.text:

Record your observations.

Identify solid F.

3 Calcium carbonate and kaolinite are both white solids found in sedimentary rocks.
Calcium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form aqueous calcium chloride. Kaolinite
does not react with dilute acids.
You are provided with a mixture of calcium carbonate and kaolinite and access to
dilute hydrochloric acid.
Plan an experiment to determine the percentage by mass of calcium carbonate in the mixture.
